messages.author: e19ea506112fd25b
messages.subject: goodness of fit/full predictive posterior/mixed predictive posterior
parts:
Hi,

I am trying to explain full predictive posterior and mixed predictive posterior plots which were generated by R from stan to my frequentist colleagues.  Can someone reference to a text where such plots are interpreted in simple terms?  As full/mixed predictive posterior I am using the definitions in the attached article (options B and C on pg 4).  My frequentist colleagues ask the question how to determine when fit is good and why.

Thanks for any help,
Linas

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] goodness of fit/full predictive posterior/mixed predictive posterior
parts:
I would suggest option A, cross-validation, which gets straight
to predictive power and is easily interpretable across frameworks.
You'd want to use full Bayesian inference for the predictions,
of course.

Between options B and C, usually the likelihood is defined by
marginalizing out the hierarchical parameters for the prediction,
so C seems more reasonable. And it's necessary to make predictions
for new groups not part of the original fit. This is tricky in more
highly structured multilevel models.

We need to add more discussion of posterior predictive checks
and cross-validation to the manual.

- Bob

Linas

parts:
It would be helpful to have an example in the manual (ultimately, in the book we plan to write) showing a Stan model with ppc. We already have the paper showing xval and waic in Stan, it would be good to see ppc as well.

Ultimately we plan to have the graphical models wrapper for Stan in R, so that will be another way to do it. But it wouldn’t be bad to have it in pure Stan, with the posterior predictive simulations right in the generated quantities, and then maybe a bit of R code showing the construction of a posterior predictive test with graph.

A
